source.title: Large-batch Optimization for Dense Visual Predictions
source.authors: Zeyue Xue; Jian-Ming Liang; Guang-Lu Song; Zhuo-Fan Zong; Liang Chen; Yu Liu; Ping Luo

record.tranche_reason: The study compares held-out dense-prediction performance across batch sizes and optimization methods, and measures module gradient variance, using tasks and measurements distinct from the claim versions’ core classification settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports dense-prediction validation performance and gradient-variance measurements. AGVM results are included where they show large-batch outcomes; AGVM is the study’s proposed method, so its method-only comparisons are not treated as independent findings about the claim.
record.test_reason: The batch-size sweeps test V5's large-batch performance effect in a new setting: dense visual prediction. Tables 2 and 3 approximately hold training-example budgets fixed by reducing iterations as batches grow; Table 5 fixes training at 24 epochs. These are extensions beyond V5's image-classification and language-model settings.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's broad paraphrase is accurate: the authors attribute large-batch difficulties in dense prediction to module gradient-variance misalignment and conclude that AGVM enables faster, more stable training across pipelines. Their descriptions of maintained performance require qualification: Table 5 reports AGVM RetinaNet mAP decreasing from 32.8 at batch 32 to 26.7 at 10k.
record.recipe_differences: The study focuses on dense visual prediction tasks and introduces module-wise gradient-variance modulation. It does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, or the claim versions’ stated classification protocols.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by batch size, pipeline, backbone, optimizer, and AGVM use. The paper also reports an ablation of anchor-module choice and changes in module gradient variance when modifying shared heads, FPN use, pixel sampling, and region proposals.

fits_no_version.finding: Large batches produce module-wise gradient-variance misalignment; architectural ablations and AGVM reduce that misalignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In modular dense visual predictors, effective-batch-size differences between modules accompany gradient-variance misalignment and poorer training outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Several large-batch configurations diverge and report NaN rather than held-out performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large batches can destabilize optimization in dense visual prediction, depending on the pipeline and optimizer.

record.problems: The study evaluates dense visual prediction tasks rather than image-classification or language-model benchmarks in V5. Table 2 labels its performance measure without specifying the metric in the supplied text. The figures show gradient-variance curves, but do not provide extractable numeric values for those curves.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 intermediate batch-size entries for several methods and pipelines, intermediate batch-size entries in Table 3, Table 4 training-time results, Table 6 optimizer/AGVM ablation results, Table 7 anchor-module results, Table 8 segmentation mAP values and training-time entries, and Table 9 hyperparameter results are not included to stay within 60 rows and prioritize batch-size endpoints, failures, and method comparisons. Figure 1, Figure 2, Figures 3–6, and associated text also report gradient-variance observations; no separate rows were retained because the plots do not provide numeric values and these results do not measure the property specified in V7.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
A controlled adaptive-versus-SGD comparison under the specified limited tuning protocol. Optimizer comparisons here use different recipes and do not establish that protocol.

Image-classification and language-model workloads; longer-training remedies; isolated normalization or regularization remedies; a general critical batch-size boundary. Training losses are not reported, so optimization failure cannot be separated from a generalization-gap mechanism.
Controlled dropout additions, removals, and interactions with training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness, training–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm or margin measures.

missing.what: Add the PMD-LAMB RetinaNet batch-32 result of 31.4 mAP, needed to interpret R43's 23.5 mAP at 4k. Correct R45 to the AGVM batch-32 result of 32.8 rather than adding a duplicate.

record.verdict_notes: AGVM batch-size sweeps bear on V5 because they measure held-out outcomes across batch sizes, beyond merely comparing the proposed method with competitors. No uncertainty estimates establish significance. Table 3 marks some values as borrowed from reference [29], but the supplied plain text loses the underlining needed to identify them; their provenance should be checked before treating every comparator value as a new result.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Widening past interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under the stated tuning conditions.
Image-classification and language-model settings; a broad workload-dependent batch-size boundary.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
